newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Aprilia motorbike maker sales, profit soar.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Aprilia motorbike maker sales, profit soar.

text.p: Italy's Aprilia, famous for its racing motorbikes, said 1996 pre-tax profit soared 74 percent to 94 billion lire ($55.7 million) on sales up 32 percent to 791 billion lire.

The company, based at Noale in the northeastern Veneto region, said in a statement that motorbike sales totalled 231,000 last year with exports rising 34 percent for a value of 359 billion lire, equal to 45 percent of overall turnover.
Aprilia, noting that the results confirmed the company's "extraordinary growth trend seen in recent years", said its main export markets continued to be Germany, Spain and France.
The company said it had reached a 24 percent share of the Italian domestic market and had increased the number of its employees to 1,275 from 818.
Aprilia chairman Ivano Beggio said growth in 1997 was continuing in line with budget forecasts despite signs of a slowdown in the motorcycle market, especially in Italy.
Beggio said the company was continuing with globalisation plans not only in commercial terms but also through possible production accords in emerging markets.
